paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. David wanted to build the house of the LORD, and God told him no. David had "shed much blood and waged great wars" (1 Chronicles 22:8). Then David did NOT pout in the corner. He gathered iron, bronze, cedar and stone, and he "made lavish preparations before his death" (1 Chronicles 22:5).

So the lesson is this: a no from God is not the end of your part. David would never lay a stone of that house, and he got to work anyway, so his son could build it. He even says, "I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 22:14). I know a little about doing work somebody else gets to enjoy, because that's a baker's life. Somebody else eats the cookie, and the baker is just happy it's warm.

And look at what David tells Solomon to hold on to: "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged" (1 Chronicles 22:13). He asks the LORD to give Solomon "insight and understanding" so he may keep the Law of the LORD (1 Chronicles 22:12). The same goes for you, baker. Whatever job God puts in your hands, set your heart to seek Him (1 Chronicles 22:19), and trust that He has already gone ahead with you.
